full_judgment:
53. To consider Dr. Hossain's submission in it's true context we found helpful guidance from the case of Khapan Bittalin co-operative society Ltd. vs. Nagendra Mahisiya Das, Supra. In that case their Lordships Fazle Hussain Muhammad Habibur Rahman and Mainur Reza Chowdhury .J, J. expressed "if fraud is proved, then there is no question of limitation and it would run from the date when fraud was detected." In our view, allegations of fraud having not been refuted, and the same having been proved, the above observation is quite pertinent. 

 57. Some of the high profile decisions where the criteria for successful review petitions have been enunciated, include the decision in the case of Mohammad Amin Khan Vs. Controller Estate Duty 14 DLR SC 276. In that case Justice Kaikaus observed, "While I would prefer not to accept those limitations as if they placed any technical obstruction in the exercise of the review jurisdiction of this Court, I would accept that they would embody the principle on which this court would not, in the exercise of such jurisdiction. It is not because a conclusion is wrong but because something obvious has been overlooked, some important aspect of the matter has not been considered, that a review petition would lie."
